programs.title: Mapping Health Hazards: From Broad Street to the Shop Floor
programs.grade_or_level: Workplace health and safety representatives, all industries
outcomes: Explain how John Snow's Broad Street pump map linked data to public health action
Identify occupational health hazards and map them like an outbreak investigator
Draft a data-backed health proposal for steward or employer review

sessions.activity: Tour the Broad Street Pump replica; read the DAO charter and discuss how mapped evidence stopped an 1854 outbreak and what a modern health-and-safety committee can learn from it.
Use the Evidence Monitor's summaries to compare historical outbreak mapping with modern workplace hazard surveillance; learners annotate one synthesis brief.
Working groups draft a hazard-mitigation proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter; learners debate it and hold a mock human-only final vote.
Review how the Progress Tracker scores outcomes; each group commits to one measurable workplace indicator to track after the program.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised hazard-map sketches (hazard type, sector, shift pattern, no names or site identifiers) contributed to a shared occupational-health evidence base.
programs.consent: Union-led consent briefing and opt-in sign-off before any data entry; site and employer names stripped; right to withdraw data at any time.

programs.title: Detective Doctors: The Pump That Saved Soho
outcomes: Retell the story of the Broad Street pump and why mapping cases mattered
Collect and plot simple health data on a neighborhood map
Distinguish what agents may do versus what people decide in the DAO

sessions.activity: Story walk at the pump replica: learners act as 1854 health detectives, tallying 'cases' on a paper map of Soho streets.
Meet the Evidence Monitor agent; learners sort claim cards into 'evidence' and 'rumor' piles to see why synthesis matters.
Working groups route 'tasks' to the right agent helper, learning how the Task Router coordinates work between decisions.
Groups propose one school or neighborhood health improvement; the class debates and votes, mirroring human-only final decisions.

programs.data_shared: Classroom tally charts of activity versus symptoms (counts only, fully aggregated, no individual records) added to a shared lesson dataset.
programs.consent: Guardian/parent consent forms required before any shared data contribution; individual answers never recorded, only class totals; learners may opt out of the tally activity.

programs.title: Evidence-to-Action: Running Agent-Supported Health Campaigns
programs.grade_or_level: NGO program staff and field coordinators, professional level
outcomes: Apply the agent-managed, human-governed model to a live public health campaign
Use synthesis briefs to ground campaign claims in evidence
Structure measurable outcomes that a Progress Tracker can report against

sessions.activity: Orientation on the charter's focus and measurable-outcome model; teams align one current NGO campaign to a charter-style outcome framework.
Hands-on with Evidence Monitor and Research Synthesis Agent outputs; teams grade the evidence behind three claims in their own campaign materials.
Collaborator Scout exercise: map potential expert collaborators and working groups; Task Router simulation assigns follow-up tasks.
Draft a funding or program proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter; peers review; simulated human steward vote closes the cycle.
Define 2-3 indicators per campaign and rehearse reading Progress Tracker dashboards for donor and board reporting.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised campaign indicator definitions and baseline values (indicator name, region type, unit) for a shared cross-NGO outcomes library.
programs.consent: MOU-based organizational consent plus individual opt-in; all beneficiary data excluded, only aggregate indicator metadata shared; withdrawal honored on request.

programs.title: Governance by Design: Humans Decide, Agents Serve
programs.grade_or_level: Nonprofit boards, trustees and executive directors
outcomes: Explain the 'agents operate; people govern' principle and its five human-reserved actions
Assess readiness to adopt agent-managed workflows under board control
Design a decision-cycle calendar with clear human checkpoints

sessions.activity: Board-level briefing at the pump replica: how the charter reserves final votes, amendments, treasury, enactment and steward appointments for humans alone.
Case study: a drafted proposal moves through agent drafting, human debate and human-only enactment; trustees mark where each reserved action occurs.
Map the nonprofit's own workflows onto Task Router and working-group structures; identify which decisions must stay human-reserved.
Build a one-page accountability dashboard from Progress Tracker outputs suitable for trustee and funder reporting.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised governance checkpoint diagrams (decision type, cycle length, veto points, no org names) for a shared governance-pattern library.
programs.consent: Board resolution authorizing participation; diagrams anonymized by an independent party; any identifying detail removed before sharing; opt-out anytime.
